issues.legal_issue: A party seeking to introduce evidence in an appeal is not disqualified from doing so under the due-diligence ground merely because it led no evidence at trial.
material_facts: A suit challenging land-acquisition proceedings and seeking an injunction was decreed ex parte.
The authority, which had been impleaded as a defendant, appealed and sought to file two documents said to show that possession had been taken from the plaintiff.
The authority had led no evidence at trial.
The High Court rejected the application solely because the authority had led no evidence at trial.
issues.conclusion: The rejection was set aside because having led no evidence at trial is not an additional bar to an application under Order 41 Rule 27(1)(aa). The High Court must consider the application on its merits and decide it in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Order 41 Rule 27(1)(aa) of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the applicant to establish that, despite due diligence, the evidence was not within its knowledge or could not have been produced at trial. It does not require the applicant to have led some evidence at trial. The Court rejected the contrary interpretations in Md. Saifur Rahman v. State of Assam and Gurbakash Singh v. (Finn) Shankar Das.

rule.if: first_appeal_pending and additional_evidence_requested and due_diligence_condition_met and no_evidence_led_at_trial

predicates.first_appeal_pending: A party is pursuing an appeal from a trial court decree.
predicates.additional_evidence_requested: A party asks the appellate court to receive evidence that was not produced at trial.
predicates.due_diligence_condition_met: The party establishes that despite due diligence the evidence was not known to it or could not have been produced at trial.
predicates.no_evidence_led_at_trial: The party seeking to introduce evidence produced no evidence at trial.

issues.definition: When a party pursuing an appeal seeks evidence that it could not know of or produce at trial despite due diligence, its failure to lead any evidence at trial does not by itself disqualify it from seeking to introduce that evidence.
